specific_competences.main_competence: Manage information search from different sources for lifelong learning
specific_competences.specific_competence: Use ICT tools to search for information from different sources
learning_activities: (a) Familiarise with various types of search engines (e.g., Google, Google Scholar, Bing)
(b) Utilise ICT tools to search for general information (e.g., books, journals)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming different types of search engines and the information they can search through them Practical: Guide the students in groups through completing web search tasks to find information on a given topic
Practical: Guide the students through completing web search tasks to find books, journals, articles, and images and storing them for use
assessment_criteria: Various types of search engines are familiarised effectively
ICT tools are utilised effectively in searching for general information
resources: Relevant texts and journals

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: . Develop listening skills
learning_activities: (a) Answer questions based on information from presentations/tasks
(b) Practise pronunciation of words from oral and audio/audio- visual sources
(c) Write words heard from oral and audio/audio- visual sources
(d) Reproduce messages from oral presentations
teaching_methods: Presentation: Make a presentation on a selected topic to the students and ask them questions Guide the students in groups through presenting topics and responding to questions from others’ presentations

Tongue twisters: Play recorded tongue twisters for students to listen and note down new words they learned to pronounce Reciting: Guide the students through reciting the tongue twisters by pronouncing words correctly Songs: Play recorded authentic songs with the appropriate pronunciations for students to listen. Then, guide the students through singing the songs by pronouncing words correctly
Dictation: Guide the students through writing the words heard from audio/ audio-visual recordings Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through writing sentences using the words heard

Imitation: Guide the students through reproducing messages from the information presented orally Whispering game/Message passing: Guide the students through listening to oral information and passing it on to others
assessment_criteria: Questions based on information from presentations/ tasks are answered correctly
Pronunciation of words from oral and audio/audio- visual sources is practised appropriately
Words heard from oral and audio/audio- visual sources are written
Messages from oral presentations are reproduced accurately
resources: Texts about a wide range of events, recorded materials on various situations, pictures, songs, tongue twisters, and language games

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Produce short and coherent oral messages with intelligible pronunciation and fluency
learning_activities: (a) Distinguish words with minimal sound distinctions that have different meanings (cut/cat; paper/ pepper; date/debt)
(b) Practise pronunciation with proper word stress assignment
(c) Practise pronunciation of words with short and long vowels (e.g., sit/seat, hit/ heat, pot/port)
(d) Practise pronunciation of unfamiliar sounds (e.g., through the use of tongue twisters, songs, poems)
(e) Practise pronunciation of words with similar sounds that have different spellings (e.g., one/won, ewe/you)
teaching_methods: Word cards: Use an appropriate number of cards to write minimal pairs and ask the students to distinguish their sounds and meanings Tongue twisters: Guide the students through pronouncing tongue twisters with minimal pairs Minimal pairs games: Guide the students through pronouncing words with nearly similar sounds by using games (e.g., Is it a pair?, odd one out, minimal pair up, minimal pair slap, minimal pairs pelmanism, and pronunciation journey)

Mimic: Use ICT to play word pronunciation with appropriate stress placement and ask the students to mimic Dictionary use: Use a dictionary to show the students how to indicate stress on syllables of words, and guide them through pronouncing the words Games: Use games like Clap or Clicking fingers on the stressed syllables and mumbling stress pattern

Mimic: Use ICT to play pronunciation of words with short and long vowels and ask the students to mimic Games: Use games like ‘Same or Different’ and ‘Pronunciation Maze’ to guide the students through pronouncing words with short and long vowels

Information search: Guide the students through searching for unfamiliar words from different sources and presenting their work to the class Tongue twisters: Guide the students through pronouncing tongue twisters with unfamiliar sounds Songs: Guide the students through singing a song with unfamiliar sounds Poems: Guide the students through reading aloud and reciting poems with unfamiliar sounds Mimic: Use ICT to play the pronunciation of unfamiliar sounds and ask the students to mimic

Drill: Guide the students through choral and individual repetition to pronounce correctly words with similar sounds Games: Guide the students through pronouncing words with similar sounds but different spellings by using games (e.g., Is it a pair?, odd one out, pelmanism and homophone go fish)
assessment_criteria: Words with minimal sound distinctions that have different meanings are distinguished correctly
Pronunciation with proper word stress assignment is practised appropriately
Pronunciation of words with short and long vowels is practised appropriately
Pronunciation of unfamiliar sounds is practised appropriately through the use of various techniques
Pronunciation of words with similar sounds but different spellings is practised appropriately
resources: Dictionaries, speakers, written texts, recorded materials on various situations, cards, tongue twisters

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Develop vocabulary from conversations and written texts
learning_activities: (a) Write new vocabulary from conversations and written texts on particular topics (e.g., politics, sports, tourism, agriculture)
(b) Construct sentences using vocabulary acquired from conversations and written texts
(c) Play vocabulary building games using digital and non-digital resources (e.g., word board games, charades, picture games, flash cards)
teaching_methods: Discussion: Guide the students through discussing a particular topic and writing the vocabulary heard and their meanings Dialogue: Guide the students through participating in a dialogue and writing new vocabulary from it Extensive reading: Guide the students through reading texts to acquire vocabulary for specific fields and writing new vocabulary

Dialogue: Guide the students through acting out a dialogue and constructing sentences using the new vocabulary learned Debate: Guide the students through participating in a debate and constructing sentences using the new vocabulary learned Spotting words: Guide the students through identifying new vocabulary from written texts and constructing sentences using the words Close reading: Guide the students through reading texts and constructing sentences using the new words learned

Games: Guide the students through playing vocabulary building games Questions and answers: Ask the students some questions about the new vocabulary they have learned Collaborative practice: Guide the students in pairs/groups through constructing sentences using the new vocabulary they have learned
assessment_criteria: New vocabulary from conversations and written texts on particular topics are written correctly
Sentences are constructed correctly using vocabulary acquired from conversations and written texts
Vocabulary building games are played accurately using digital and non-digital resources
resources: Audio and audio-visual materials, texts of different types, dictionaries

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary in oral and in written language tasks
learning_activities: (a) Express ideas or opinions in contextualised oral and written language tasks using proper grammar and vocabulary (e.g hospital, market, library, bus stop, sport and games)

(b) Construct sentences using appropriate grammar and vocabulary relating to a specific context (structure: tenses – simple past, simple present, articles, present progressive, pronouns, coordinators, prepositions, adjectives, adverbs)
(c) Debate on topics using proper grammar and vocabulary
teaching_methods: Conversations: Guide the students through expressing their opinions orally and in writing by participating in conversations (e.g., discussion, debate, dialogue, bargaining) on controversial issues Scenario: Present some controversial cases and ask the students to discuss and express their opinions orally and in writing. Roleplay: Guide the students through roleplaying radio/TV programmes by giving opinions on given topics

Description: Guide the students through describing objects, events, and places using appropriate grammar and vocabulary Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through writing sentences in different tenses and discussing why the sentences are written in those tenses Group work: Guide the students in groups through constructing sentences orally and in writing which describe qualities using pronouns, coordinators, prepositions, adjectives and adverbs
Debates: Guide the students through conducting debates on cross-cutting topics using proper grammar and vocabulary
assessment_criteria: Ideas or opinions are expressed correctly in contextualised oral and written language tasks using proper grammar and vocabulary
Sentences are constructed correctly using appropriate grammar and vocabulary relating to a specific context
Topics are debated appropriately using proper grammar and vocabulary
resources: Audio and audio-visual materials (audio clips, recorded stories), texts of different types, dictionaries

specific_competences.specific_competence: Read texts for comprehension
learning_activities: (a) Sequence the order of events in stories
(b) Make a summary of stories
(c) Retell stories
teaching_methods: Reading stories: Guide the students through reading stories with sequence words. (e.g., next, then, after, earlier, first, second, and later) Then, ask them to identify the words and use them to write a paragraph Filling the missing parts: Give the students stories with skipped parts and ask them to fill in the missing parts using sequence words Strip story: Guide the students through sequencing the order of events in stories using strip story. Then, let them read their stories aloud in the classroom Story completion: Provide the students with a beginning part of a story and guide them through completing it using sequence words Jumbled texts: Use jumbled texts to guide the students through ordering the sequence of events in the stories

Discussion: Guide the students through discussing the main issues in a story 5Ws and 1H, First Then Finally, SWBST, and SAAC Method: Guide the students through summarising various stories using the aforementioned methods

Retelling stories: Guide the students in pairs through retelling stories by taking turns Narration: Guide the students through narrating to others about story books and appropriate movies they have watched
assessment_criteria: The order of events in a story is sequenced logically
Stories are summarised correctly
Stories are retold accordingly
resources: A variety of texts, selected class readers, newspaper articles, journals, encyclopaedia

specific_competences.specific_competence: Comprehend oral messages with increasing difficulty
learning_activities: (a) Paraphrase various oral messages from different contexts
(b) Respond to oral messages from different contexts
(c) Respond to questions about oral messages
teaching_methods: Paraphrasing: Read passages orally, play recorded texts and guide the students through paraphrasing the messages Project: Ask the students to listen to various oral messages (presentations, on radio, TV) and paraphrase the messages for presentation in the classroom

Roleplay: Guide the students through roleplay to respond to oral instructions, information and orders Telephone conversation: Guide the students through responding to interrogations via telephone conversations
Panel interviews: Guide the students through responding to questions in panel interviews
assessment_criteria: Various oral messages are paraphrased appropriately from different contexts
Oral messages from different contexts are responded to correctly
Questions about oral messages are responded to correctly
resources: Oral and written texts, audio and audio-visual materials (audio clips, recorded stories),

specific_competences.specific_competence: Respond appropriately in a variety of oral and written communication contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express ideas and opinions in different interpersonal communication settings (e.g., I think…, I guess…, In my opinion…, I would say …)
(b) Use appropriate non-verbal cues in interpersonal communication
(c) Use proper grammar and vocabulary in different interpersonal communication contexts (e.g., greetings, biding farewell, apologising)
(d) Use appropriate language and expressions in communicating with people of different age groups and statuses (e.g., peers, elders, family members, leaders)
teaching_methods: Information search: Guide the students through seeking information on expressing ideas and opinions in interpersonal communication Scenario: Use a controversial scenario to guide the students through expressing their opinions orally and in writing

Discussion: Guide the students through discussing the meaning of different non- verbal cues and presenting the work to the class Act it out: Guide the students in groups through acting and interpreting non- verbal cues
Roleplay: Guide the students through roleplaying greeting guests, bidding farewell and apologising using proper grammar and vocabulary

Brainstorming: Guide the students in groups through brainstorming ideas on the differences in conversations between different groups of people Dialogue: Guide the students through participating in dialogue among different age groups and statuses
assessment_criteria: Ideas and opinions are expressed correctly in different interpersonal communication settings
Appropriate non- verbal cues are used correctly in interpersonal communication
Grammar and vocabulary are used correctly in different interpersonal communication contexts
Appropriate language and expressions are used with different age groups and statuses
resources: Dictionaries, a variety of texts

specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary for oral communication in a variety of contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express daily routines (structure: present simple)
(b) Express ongoing activities (structure: present progressive)
(c) Express family relationship and occupations (structure: present simple+progressive)
(d) Express ownership/ possession (structure: have/has in present simple and had in past simple, apostrophe, possessive pronouns)
(e) Give directions
teaching_methods: Real-life expression: Guide the students through expressing orally what they do usually Inquiry: Guide the students through inquiring what famous people in their community do usually and presenting their work before the class Interview: Guide the students in pairs through interviewing each other about their fact routines

Description: Guide the students through describing events as they occur (e.g., wedding ceremonies, birthday parties, burial ceremonies, processes, and public events) using the present progressive tense

Brainstorming: Guide the students in pairs through brainstorming ideas about family relationship and different kinds of occupations Songs and games: Guide the students through singing songs and playing games about family relationships and occupations Matching: Guide the students through matching pictures with occupations and occupations with their descriptions The use of pictures: Display pictures of people with different occupations and ask the students to express their occupations using the present simple+progressive tenses Real-life expression: Ask the students to express the occupations of their parents/ guardians and other relatives using the present simple+progressive tenses

Information search: Guide the students through reading texts on expressing possession using have, has, had, apostrophe, and possessive pronouns Real-life expression: Guide the students through expressing possessions using the real objects they posses Conversation: Guide the students in groups through engaging in conversations about what their relatives and neighbours posses

Information search: Guide the students through searching for information on how to ask for and give directions and present the work to the class Map reading: Guide the students in pairs through directing each other how to reach various stations/points (from one point to another) as indicated in the map Group work: Guide the students in groups through asking and giving directions on how to reach various places (e.g., offices, classrooms, and toilets) within the school compound
assessment_criteria: Daily routines are expressed correctly
Ongoing activities are expressed correctly
Family relationship and occupations are expressed correctly
Ownership/ possession is expressed correctly
Directions are given appropriately
resources: Dictionaries, relevant texts, pictures, maps of various places (e.g., school, village)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Create a variety of texts for different communicative purposes using the appropriate tone and register
learning_activities: (a) Recognise the main stages of writing texts (e.g., pre- writing, drafting, revising, editing)
(b) Write a variety of friendly letters and invitations (vocabulary: Dear Father/ Uncle, Dear Mother/Aunt, Mr/Mrs…, Dr./ Prof./Madam/Ms …)
(c) Create dialogues on various topics (e.g., the value of education, environment, culture, gender equality)
(d) Create and express orally daily and weekly timetables for routines
teaching_methods: Discussion: Guide the students through discussing stages of writing texts and presenting their work to the class Demonstration: Demonstrate how to begin writing by asking the students to give ideas and help you plan the text

Observation: Display/distribute samples of friendly letters and invitations for the students to study and discover their parts Collaboration: Guide the students through collaborating in writing friendly letters and invitations

Brainstorming: Guide the students in groups through brainstorming ideas on the meaning and structure of dialogues Observation: Guide the students through studying a prepared dialogue and writing down the key features they observe Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through creating dialogues on various topics Act it out: Guide the students in pairs through acting out the dialogues they have prepared

Real-life expression: Guide the students through expressing orally and in writing what they do weekly Inquiry: Guide the students through inquiring what famous people do weekly and reporting to the classroom Interview: Guide the students through interviewing each other in pairs about their fact routines and timetables Planning and preparing: Guide the students individually through planning and preparing their weekly timetables and presenting them to the class
assessment_criteria: The stages of writing texts are recognised appropriately
A variety of friendly letters and invitations are written correctly with appropriate vocabulary
Dialogues on various topics are created appropriately
Daily and weekly time- tables for routines are created and expressed correctly
resources: Relevant texts, dictionaries, samples of friendly letters and invitations

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Develop listening skills
learning_activities: (a) Participate in various conversations in different communicative settings (e.g., peer discussions, storytelling)
(b) Summarise information from oral presentations and audio/audio- visual sources
(c) Paraphrase information presented orally
teaching_methods: Discussion: Guide the students through discussing various cross-cutting issues, noting down important ideas and presenting the work to the class Storytelling: Ask the students in pairs to tell stories by taking turns, write down important ideas and present them to the class Dialogue: Guide the students through acting out a dialogue on various interesting events (football matches, tourism trips, visits to grandparents, and school leaders’ election) and ask them questions from the dialogue Interview: Guide some students (inteviewers) through inteviewing others (interviewee) on various issues/topics Round table circle: Guide the students through participating in discussion on the selected topics using the round table circle and presenting their work to the class

Presentation: Make a presentation on any interesting topic and ask the students to listen to it attentively Discussion: Guide the students through discussing and summarising the information from the presentation, and presenting their work to the class Recordings: Guide the students through summarising recorded information (e.g., recorded song, dialogue, speech and interview) played in class using digital devices (e.g., smartphone, tablet, computer, radio). Then, ask each them to present their work through gallery walk Project activity: Ask the students to listen to and watch the news on the radio and TV respectively at home and school. Then, ask them to summarise the news broadcast and present the work to the class

Narrating stories: Narrate an interesting story to the students, and guide them through paraphrasing information from the story and presenting their work to the class Project activity: Guide the students through paraphrasing the news broadcast they have listened to on radio and watched on TV at home or school and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: Participations in conversations in various communicative settings is done effectively
Information from oral presentations and audio/audio- visual sources is summarised logically
Information presented orally is paraphrased correctly
resources: Texts of a wide range of events, pictures and recorded materials on various situations, songs, language games

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Produce short and coherent oral messages with intelligible pronunciation and fluency
learning_activities: (a) Construct sentences with proper intonation
(b) Use cohesive devices to deliver oral presentations of events (e.g., first of all, moreover, but, however, yet, in contrast, although, otherwise, still, on the contrary, on the other hand)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming various communication contexts/ settings (e.g., market, sports and games, hospital, restaurant/hotel) and identifying vocabulary used in such contexts/settings Sentence construction: Guide the students through constructing sentences orally using the identified vocabulary Scenario/case study: Guide the students through using some vocabulary and grammatical items from a scenario/case study to construct different sentences orally
Discussion: Guide the students in pairs through preparing and making presentations using cohesive devices
assessment_criteria: Sentences with proper intonation are constructed appropriately
Cohesive devices are used to deliver oral presentations logically
resources: Dictionaries, speakers, written texts, recorded materials on various situations

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Develop vocabulary from conversations and written texts
learning_activities: (a) Recognise words with opposite meanings from conversations and written texts
(b) Use words from conversations and written texts to produce new vocabulary by attaching suffixes and prefixes (e.g., kind-unkind; slow-slowly)
teaching_methods: Roleplay: Use a roleplay to guide the students in pairs or in groups through acting out different roles. (e.g., doctor and patient, teacher and student, chairperson and villagers) TIPS: Provide the students with some words from the roleplay and guide them through TIPS to find their opposite meanings and use them to construct sentences Hot seat: Guide the students through using the hot seat to ask and respond to questions based on the topics provided to them Brainstorming: Ask the students to brainstorm the opposite meanings of some words used in the hot seat and use them to construct sentences Discussion: Provide the students with texts to read, discuss their contents and make presentations Memory card game: Guide the students through recognising words with opposite meanings from the texts read by playing the memory card game, finding their meanings and using them to construct sentences

Talk show: Guide the students through participating in talk shows on different topics/themes and using some vocabulary from the talk shows to produce new vocabulary by attaching suffixes and prefixes and then constructing sentences using the new vocabulary learned Prefix and suffix bingo: Use the prefix and suffix bingo to guide the students through forming new vocabulary. Then, ask them to construct sentences using the new vocabulary
assessment_criteria: Words with opposite meanings from conversations and written texts are recognised
New vocabulary is correctly formed from conversations and written texts by attaching suffixes and prefixes
resources: Audio and audio-visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories), texts of different types, dictionaries, encyclopaedia, thesaurus

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary in oral and in written language tasks
learning_activities: (a) Produce contextualised oral and written descriptions based on personal experience

(b) Compose passages on specific contexts (structure: tenses –past progressive, present perfect, past perfect, present progressive, adjectives, adverbs, coordinators, prepositions, determiners, conjunctions)
(c) Present messages in formal discussions on various issues using correct grammar and vocabulary
teaching_methods: Description: Guide the students through describing different events, places, and living and non-living things based on their experience orally and in writing using descriptive words

Jumbled sentences/paragraphs: Ask the students to rewrite jumbled sentences/paragraphs to form a meaningful passage about a specific context Brainstorming: Guide the students in pairs through brainstorming different contexts for composing passages and presenting their work to the class Discussion: Guide the students in groups through discussing important considerations when composing passages. Then, let each group present its work to the class Composing: Guide the students through composing passages on the chosen contexts using appropriate grammar and vocabulary

Discussion: Provide the students with topics to discuss using correct grammar and vocabulary in initiating, intervening in and closing the discussions Round table circle: Guide the students through participating in discussion on the selected topic using the round table circle and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: Oral and written descriptions based on personal experience are produced logically
Passages on specific contexts are composed well
Messages in formal discussions on various issues using correct grammar and vocabulary are presented rationally
resources: Audio and audio-visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories), texts of different types, dictionaries, head set, media player/ recorder

specific_competences.specific_competence: Read texts for comprehension
learning_activities: (a) Express the main ideas from a text
(b) Infer meanings of unfamiliar words and idiomatic expressions from a given text
(c) Relate the core messages from a text to real life experiences
teaching_methods: Discussion: Guide the students through identifying and discussing the main ideas of the texts read, and expressing the identified ideas orally and in writing
Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through inferring the meanings of unfamiliar words and idiomatic expressions from a given text and presenting their work to the class
Group work: Provide the students with texts to read in groups, identify the core messages of the texts, relate them with their life experiences and present the work to the class
assessment_criteria: The main ideas of texts are expressed properly
The meanings of unfamiliar words and idiomatic expressions from a given text are inferred accurately
The core messages from a text are related reasonably to real-life experiences
resources: A variety of texts, selected poems, newspaper articles, journals, encyclopaedia, books

specific_competences.specific_competence: Comprehend oral messages with increasing difficulty
learning_activities: (a) Synthesise ideas from a variety of oral sources
(b) Summarise information from a variety of oral sources
(c) Participate in contextualised oral conversations
teaching_methods: Songs: Sing or play a song to the students while they listen to it attentively Presentation: Present a topic or read aloud a passage/story to the students while they listen to it attentively Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through synthesising ideas from the song and presentation or passage/story they have listened to. Then, let each pair present its work to the class Discussion: Guide the students through discussing and synthesising ideas from various oral sources (e.g., radio, audio and video clips, television). Then, let each group present the work to the class

Presentation: Present a topic or read aloud a passage to the students and guide them through identifying the main ideas from the presentation or passage, summarising the presentation or passage and presenting their work to the class Songs: Sing or play a song to the students and guide them through identifying the main ideas and summarising information from the song. Let each group present the work to the class Audio/audio-visual: Guide the students through summarising information from other oral sources (e.g., radio, audio and video clips, television) and presenting the work to the class

Debate: Guide the students through participating in debates on various topics Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out a dialogue about a specific context Roleplay: Guide the students in pairs or in groups through acting out different roles. (e.g., doctor and patient, teacher and student, chairperson and villagers). Jigsaw: Provide the students with topics, including cross-cutting issues, and guide them through the jigsaw to discuss such topics Round table circle: Guide the students through participating in discussion on various topics using the round table circle and presenting their work to the class Pub quiz: Let two groups sit together and take turns to pose questions to each other on the selected topic. Each group agree or disagree on the answers provided
assessment_criteria: Ideas from a variety of oral sources are synthesised correctly
Information from a variety of oral sources is summarised clearly
Participations in contextualised oral conversations are done effectively
resources: Oral texts, audio and audio-visual materials (audio and video clips)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Respond appropriately in a variety of oral and written communication contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express ideas and opinions in different group communicative settings (differing, counter-arguing, supporting ideas)
(b) Use appropriate non-verbal cues in group communication
(c) Use appropriate language to respond to messages in online group communicative contexts (e.g., WhatsApp, Telegram)
teaching_methods: Talk show: Guide the students through TV or radio talk show to express their ideas, opinions and facts on a controversial or opinion topic Discussion: Guide the students through discussing a controversial or opinion topic by expressing their ideas, opinions and facts in writing and publishing their works on social media or in the school magazine

Discussion: Provide the students with topics to discuss and guide them through using appropriate non-verbal cues where applicable Presentation: Guide each group through presenting its work and using appropriate non-verbal cues in their presentations Roleplay: Use a roleplay to guide the students in pairs or in groups through acting out different roles. (e.g., doctor and patient, teacher and student, chairperson and villagers) using non-verbal cues appropriately where applicable Debate: Guide the students through participating in debates on various topics using non-verbal cues where applicable

Group chat/communication: Guide the students in groups through choosing topics for communication. (e.g., Class meeting) Then, provide them with paper and guide them through exchanging their ideas on the paper using appropriate language—As it is done on WhatsApp, Telegram). Note: If applicable, guide them through using smartphones or tablets
assessment_criteria: Opinions and facts in mass communication are expressed clearly
Non-verbal cues in group communication are used appropriately
The appropriate language is used in online group communicative contexts
resources: Dictionaries, a variety of texts, audio and audiovisual materials

specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary for oral communication in a variety of contexts
learning_activities: (a) Describe various locations (structure: prepositions, adjectives, adverbs)
(b) Express quality and quantity of objects and living organisms (structure: adjectives, quantifiers, adverbs)
(c) Negotiate prices using appropriate expressions (e.g., convincing a customer to buy a product, convincing a seller to lower the price) (Structure: May I…, I would like…, could you …, I offer you…)
(d) Request for services in different contexts
(e) Participate in various conversations in different contexts (e.g., discussions, dialogues) by initiating, intervening, changing a topic, turn-taking and closing
teaching_methods: Description: Guide the students through describing various locations orally (e.g., towns, streets, markets, and hospitals) using appropriate grammar and vocabulary
Description: Guide the students through describing various objects and living organisms orally

Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out a dialogue based on the context of the market where a seller convinces a customer to buy a product, and a customer convinces a seller to lower the price Roleplay: Assign the students in pairs the role of seller and customer and guide them through acting out such roles using appropriate grammar and vocabulary Discussion: Guide the students through discussing what has been roleplayed and presenting their work to the class

Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out a dialogue based on requesting for services Roleplay: Guide the students in pairs through roleplaying to request services and provide such services in different contexts Discussion: Guide the students through discussing what has been roleplayed and presenting their work through a gallery walk

Discussion: Guide the students through discussing various topics using appropriate language when initiating, intervening in, changing a topic, taking turns and closing their discussions Jigsaw: Guide the students through jigsaw to discuss various topics, including cross-cutting issues Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out dialogues in different contexts Interview: Let some students (the interviewers) interview others (the interviewees) on various issues/ topics (e.g., Job interview and panel interview) Talk show: Guide the students in groups through preparing and participating in short talk shows on the chosen topics/themes Hot seat: Let some students interview others on the chosen topics/themes through the hot seat
assessment_criteria: Various locations are described well
Qualities and quantities of objects and living organisms are expressed correctly
Negotiations over the price using appropriate expressions are done
Requests for services in different contexts are done correctly
Participations in various conversations in different contexts by initiating, intervening, changing a topic, turn-taking, closing are done
resources: Recorded materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories), on various situations

specific_competences.specific_competence: Create a variety of texts for different communicative purposes using the appropriate tone and register
learning_activities: (a) Write claim and request letters in different contexts (e.g., learning facilities, sports gear, result report – Structure: I would like to bring your kind attention… I am writing to request…)
(b) Compose E-mails on various issues using appropriate language
(c) Create short stories on various topics (structure: once upon a time …, I wonder…, what if…, back in time…)
teaching_methods: Discussion: Guide the students through discussing things to consider in writing official letters, including claim and request letters and presenting the work to the class Letter writing: Guide the students through writing claim and request letters on various situations using appropriate language

Gallery walk: Guide the students through a gallery walk to discuss and present components of email and important things to consider when composing emails Composing: Guide the students through composing emails on various issues

Demonstration: Choose a topic and demonstrate how to create short stories step-by-step Story completion: Create a short story for some sentences or paragraphs and guide the students through completing writing the story and reading aloud their work to the class Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through creating short stories on the topics of their interest and reading aloud their stories to the class. Then, check the correctness of the created stories based on various factors (e.g., language used, series of events, coherence)
assessment_criteria: Claim and request letters in different contexts are written correctly
Emails on various issues are composed using appropriate language
Short stories on various topics are created
resources: Relevant texts, dictionaries, samples of claim and request letters

specific_competences.main_competence: Manage information search from different sources for lifelong learning
specific_competences.specific_competence: Organise information obtained from different sources
learning_activities: (a) Identify different ways/strategies for organising information from various sources
(b) Sort and categorise information obtained from various sources into related themes
(c) Compile information searched from various sources
teaching_methods: Information search: Guide the students through searching for different ways/ strategies for organising information from various sources and presenting their work to the class
I do, we do, you do (Gradual release of responsibility): Guide the students through using the “I do, we do, you do” method to sort and categorise information obtained from various sources

Project: Assign the students a project work to search for information from different sources I do, we do, you do: Guide the students through using the “I do, we do, you do” method to compile the information searched on various sources
assessment_criteria: Strategies for organising information from various sources are identified
Information obtained from various sources is sorted and categorized appropriately into related themes
Information searched from various sources is compiled properly
resources: Journals, written texts, newspapers, encyclopedias, magazines

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary in oral and in written language tasks
learning_activities: (a) Hold conversations about various contexts using appropriate grammar and vocabulary (structure: tenses, adverbs, adjectives, active and passive voice, conjunctions, coordinators, prepositions)
(b) Compose stories using proper grammar and vocabulary (structure: tenses, adverbs, adjectives, active and passive voice, conjunctions, coordinators, prepositions)
(c) Describe events (e.g., general elections, state funerals, world cup) using correct grammar and vocabulary
teaching_methods: Scenario: Give the students a scenario to share ideas in groups using conversation techniques, appropriate grammar and vocabulary Debates: Guide the students through developing topics for conversations and participating in debates on the topics Interviews: Guide the students through preparing and participating in community interviews about community needs, concerns and expectations Telephoning: Guide the students through making telephone conversations on various topics using appropriate grammar and vocabulary

Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming ideas on the main parts of stories and reading stories with appreciation Story mapping: Guide the students through planning the structure of stories using a story map graphic organiser. Composition: Guide the students through using their story plans to compose stories using proper grammar and vocabulary and sharing the stories for discussion

Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming ideas on the main issues to include when describing provided events and presenting them to the class Talk show: Guide the students through preparing scripts for talk shows to describe events and participating in the talk shows Description: Guide the students through describing events orally and in writing using correct grammar and vocabulary
assessment_criteria: Conversations about various contexts using appropriate grammar and vocabulary are held
Stories using proper grammar and vocabulary are composed
Events are described by using correct grammar and vocabulary
resources: Written texts of different types, dictionaries, encyclopaedias, oral texts, audio and audio - visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Read texts for comprehension
learning_activities: (a) Distinguish facts from opinions within a given text
(b) Express connotative meanings of words in relation to a text
(c) Paraphrase a given text
teaching_methods: Questions and answers: Present statements in class and ask the students to decide whether the statements are facts or opinions and give reasons for their responses Reading: Guide the students through extracting parts which represent facts and opinions in written texts Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through writing short passages by including facts and opinions

Discussion: Guide the students through discussing and providing examples of connotative meanings of words in relation to the texts read, interpreting such meanings and presenting the work to the class

Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming ideas on the differences between paraphrasing and summarising and presenting such differences to the class Snowball discussions: Guide the students through the snowball discussions to discuss the techniques for paraphrasing Paraphrasing: Guide the students through paraphrasing texts from different sources orally and in writing using appropriate techniques
assessment_criteria: Facts and opinions within a given text are distinguished correctly
Connotative meanings of words in relation to a text are expressed appropriately
A given text is paraphrased correctly
resources: Books, dictionaries, encyclopaedia, newspaper articles, journals

specific_competences.specific_competence: Comprehend oral messages with increasing difficulty
learning_activities: (a) Discuss information from various oral sources
(b) Respond to various oral messages
(c) Make comments on oral messages
teaching_methods: Discussions: Read passages aloud and play recorded information. Then, guide the students through discussing the information heard and presenting the work to the class Interview: Guide the students in pairs or groups through participating in interviews on topical issues Project work: Ask the students to listen to and watch various oral sources (radio, TV), discuss the information heard, and present their work to the class

Roleplay: Guide the students through roleplay to respond to oral instructions (e.g., instruction manual and computer application), announcements and advertisements Interviews: Guide the students through preparing and participating in field specific interviews (e.g., journalism, sports, and politics)

Investigation: Guide the students in pairs or groups through investigating techniques to comment on messages and presenting them to the class Songs/reading aloud: Sing a song or read aloud a text for students to listen. Then, guide them in groups through commenting on its messages and presenting their comments to the class Presentation: Play a recorded presentation/speech for students to listen to and guide them in groups through commenting on its messages and presenting it to the class
assessment_criteria: Information from various oral sources is discussed appropriately
Various oral messages are responded to accordingly
Oral messages are commented on precisely
resources: Oral texts, audio and audio-visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Respond appropriately in a variety of oral and written communication contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express ideas, opinions and facts in mass communication contexts
(b) Use and interpret appropriate non- verbal cues in mass communication
(c) Use appropriate language to respond to contextualised public messages (e.g., responding to criticism, accomplishment)
(d) Use appropriate language in public communication settings, (e.g., interviews, presentations)
(e) Express appreciation of other people’s ideas in public communication
(f) Evaluate information received through mass communication
teaching_methods: Talk show: Guide the students through TV or radio talk show to express their ideas, opinions and facts on a controversial or opinion topic Discussion: Guide the students through discussing a controversial or opinion topic by expressing their ideas, opinions and facts in writing and publishing their works on social media or in the school magazine

Watching TV programmes/shows: Guide the students through watching TV programmes/shows, identifying and interpreting non-verbal cues used in the programmes/shows, and presenting their work to the class Group work: Guide the students in groups through using non-verbal cues in writing information and presenting their work to the class

Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming ideas on the criticisms, accomplishment they/ others have experienced and how they responded to them, and presenting the work to the class Group work: Guide the students in groups by taking turns through expressing their personal experiences, criticising and responding to criticisms appropriately

Interview: Guide the students through preparing and participating in interviews (e.g., panel interview, job interview, group interview, community interview) Presentations: Guide the students through preparing and making presentations on various topics Debate: Guide the students through preparing debates and participating in such debates

Gallery walk: Guide the students in groups through gallery walk to discuss and present words/expressions used in appreciating other people’s ideas Dialogue: Guide the students through preparing and acting out a dialogue whose participants appreciate each other’s ideas

TIPS: Guide the students through TIPS to identify issues to consider in evaluating information from mass communication (e.g., radio, television, newspapers, magazines, and social media) Modelling: Show the students how to evaluate information from mass communication (Use newspapers or magazines or information from radio/TV). Shared practice: Collaborate with the students to evaluate information from newspapers, magazines, or radio/TV Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through evaluating information from newspapers and magazines or radio/TV
assessment_criteria: Opinions and facts in mass communication are expressed clearly
Non-verbal cues in mass communication are interpreted and used appropriately
Contextualized public messages are responded to by using appropriate language
Language in public communication/ settings is used appropriately
Appreciations of other people’s ideas in public communication are expressed suitably
Information received through mass communication is evaluated appropriately
resources: Dictionaries, a variety of texts, audio and audio- visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Construct meaning from a variety of texts
learning_activities: (a) Compare ideas from various texts
(b) Read and generate meanings from a variety of texts
(c) Infer meanings of unfamiliar words from a variety of texts
(d) Paraphrase textual information from multiple sources
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming how to compare ideas from various texts and presenting their work to the class Close reading: Provide the students with various texts to read and guide them through comparing ideas from the texts read

Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through identifying different types of meaning and presenting their works to the class Discussion: Guide the students through reading a variety of texts, discussing different meanings contained in the texts and presenting their works to the class

Modelling: Show the students how to infer meanings of unfamiliar words from a variety of texts (Use different clues, including contextual meaning) Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through inferring meanings of unfamiliar words using insights from the texts read

I do, we do, you do: Modelling: Show the students how to paraphrase textual information from multiple sources using different techniques Shared practice: Collaborate with the students to paraphrase textual information from multiple sources using different techniques Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through paraphrasing textual information from multiple sources using different techniques
assessment_criteria: Ideas from various texts are compared correctly
Meanings from a variety of texts are generated
Meanings of unfamiliar words from a variety of texts are inferred correctly
Textual information from multiple sources is paraphrased properly
resources: Books, dictionaries, encyclopaedia, newspaper articles, journals

specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary for oral communication in a variety of contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express opinions through debates, dialogues and impromptu speeches using formulaic language (e.g., In my opinion…, personally…, I think …, I would say…, In my view…, from my perspective…, My point is…, It seems to me that…, I believe…)
(b) Present facts logically using appropriate formulaic language (e.g., due to the fact that…, it is true that…, the bottom line is…, the reality is…, in fact…actually… according to…)
(c) Describe conditions about various situations and circumstances (structure: conditional sentences)
(d) Ask and respond to questions in interview sessions (e.g., job interview, panel interview, TV/radio interview)
(e) Describe activities and events of a social or cultural nature (e.g., celebrations, parades, accidents, elections, funerals, sport and games) using different tenses
teaching_methods: Debate: Guide the students through using formulaic language to give their opinions in debates Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out a dialogue with an opinion topic Delivering impromptu speeches: Guide the students through delivering impromptu speeches on opinion topics using formulaic language

Presentation: Guide the students through preparing and making presentations with factual information using formulaic language Debate: Guide the students through participating in debates and using formulaic language to present facts

Investigation: Guide the students through investigating the structure of conditional sentences and presenting the work to the class Chain conditionals (Conditional train): Guide the students through constructing conditional sentences orally using chain conditionals Pelmanism (Concentration) game: Guide the students through playing the pelmanism game to construct conditional sentences orally Mill drill questionnaire (Mingling activities) Guide the students through constructing conditional sentences orally using the mill drill questionnaire Group discussion: Assign the students roles to play (e.g., politicians, teachers, traffic police) and provide them with the same questions to discuss based on the particular roles Songs: Guide the students through singing songs with conditionals and identifying the conditionals in the songs

Modelling: Use recorded interview sessions on different topics to model students on how to ask and respond to interview questions Interview/roleplay: Guide the students through engaging in interviews by roleplaying the role of interviewees and interviewers

Description: Guide the students in groups to take turns and describe orally social and cultural activities, or events they have participated in or witnessed. Then, guide them through describing orally such activities and events in the classroom.
assessment_criteria: Opinions are expressed through debates, dialogues, and impromptu speeches using formulaic language
Facts are logically presented using appropriate formulaic language
Conditions about various situations and circumstances are described appropriately
Interview questions are asked and responded to correctly
Social- cultural activities and events are described properly
resources: Speakers, recorded materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories) on various situations

specific_competences.specific_competence: Create a variety of texts for different communicative purposes using the appropriate tone and register
learning_activities: (a) Write a letter to the editor, an order letter and a complaint letter (structure: Dear editor.., I would like to order…. We are glad to place our first order…, I am writing to complain about…, I am writing to bring your attention…, a complaint against…)
(b) Write reports on various events (e.g., sports, graduation, study tours)
(c) Write biographies (structure: past and present tense, third person)
teaching_methods: Observation and discussion: Guide the students through studying letters to the editor, order letters and complaint letters and discussing important considerations when writing such letters Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through writing letters to the editor, order letters and complaint letters using appropriate grammar and vocabulary

Observation/team building game: Guide the students through studying reports on various events, discussing their different aspects, including parts of the reports and the language used and presenting their work to the class Project activity: Guide the students through observing live events or participating in such events, writing reports on them, and presenting the work to the class

Biographies: Guide the students through reading and summarising biographies of famous people in writing Biography graphic organisers: Guide the students through the use of biography graphic organisers to write biographies of famous people
assessment_criteria: Letter to the editor, order and complaint letters are written correctly
Reports on various events are written appropriately
Biographies are written correctly
resources: Relevant texts, dictionaries, samples of letter to the editor, order and complaint letters

specific_competences.main_competence: Provide basic English language services to the community
specific_competences.specific_competence: Apply principles of editing and proofreading in a variety of texts
learning_activities: (a) Recognise the basic principles of editing and proofreading texts (e.g., sentence construction, language clarity, grammar, semantic rules, logical flow)
(b) Describe the main steps of editing and proofreading
(c) Describe the basic principles and methods of editing and proofreading
(d) Use the principles of editing and proofreading to edit and proofread simple and short texts in a school context (e.g., laboratory rules, announcements)
teaching_methods: Snowball discussions: Guide the students through discussing the basic principles of editing and proofreading using snowball discussions
Assignment: Assign the students a task to find the main steps in editing and proofreading, and present their work to the class
Description: Guide the students through describing the basic principles and methods of editing and proofreading, and presenting their work to the class

Modelling: Engage the students by showing them how to edit and proofread texts Shared practice: Work with the students to edit and proofread a text Collaborative and independent practice: Provide the students in pairs and individually with simple and short texts in the school context and guide them through editing and proofreading the texts
assessment_criteria: The basic principles of editing and proofreading are recognised
The main steps in editing and proofreading are described accurately
The basic principles and methods of editing and proofreading are described properly
The principles of editing and proofreading simple texts in the school context are used appropriately
resources: Relevant texts, school rules and regulations, fliers, user manuals, various essays/ compositions, dictionaries

specific_competences.main_competence: Provide basic English language services to the community
specific_competences.specific_competence: Apply principles of interpretation to provide simple authentic interpretations
learning_activities: (a) Explain the concept of interpretation
(b) Elaborate the principles of interpretation
(c) Interpret a short simple text in a school context (e.g., greetings, self introductions) (English to Kiswahili and vice versa)
teaching_methods: Know Want Learned (KWL) chart: Guide the students through using KWL chart to get their prior knowledge, expectations and what they have learnt about the concept of interpretation Group work: Guide the students through explaining the concept of interpretation and presenting their work to the class
Information search: Guide the students through searching for information about the principles of interpretation and presenting their work to the class
Simultaneous and consecutive interpretation: Guide the students in pairs through interpreting messages in the school context using simultaneous and consecutive interpretation
assessment_criteria: The concept of interpretation is explained accurately
The principles of interpretation are elaborated precisely
Short messages in the school context are interpreted appropriately
resources: Dictionaries, oral texts, audio and audio- visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.main_competence: Provide basic English language services to the community
specific_competences.specific_competence: Apply principles of translation to produce simple authentic translation
learning_activities: (a) Explain the concept of translation
(b) Elaborate the principles of translation
(c) Translate a simple short text in a school context (e.g., laboratory rules, timetables, joining instructions) (English to Kiswahili and vice versa)
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students in groups through brainstorming the concept of translation and presenting their work to the class
Discussion: Guide the students through discussing the principles of translation and presenting their work to the class

I do, we do, you do: Modelling: Engage the students by showing them how to translate texts through communicative translation. (Use a text in the school context) Shared practice: Work with the students to use communicative translation to translate a text in the school context. Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through translating texts in the school context using communicative translation
assessment_criteria: The concept of translation is explained correctly
The principles of translation are elaborated correctly
Texts in the school context are translated correctly
resources: Dictionaries, a variety of texts

specific_competences.specific_competence: Appreciate the aesthetics and value of literature
learning_activities: (a) Assess the language used in selected poems and plays
(b) Compare own values and perspectives with those implied in selected poems and plays
teaching_methods: Brainstorming: Guide the students in groups through brainstorming the language used in poems and plays, and presenting their work to the class Shared practice: Select a poem and a play, and collaborate with the students to assess the language used Collaborative and independent practice: Provide the students in pairs/ groups and individually with poems and plays to read and guide them through assessing the language used

TIPS: Guide the students through identifying own values and perspectives using TIPS Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through comparing own values and perspectives with those implied in the selected poems and plays, and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: The language used in selected poems and plays is assessed appropriately.
Own values and perspectives are compared appropriately with those implied in selected poems and plays
resources: Literary texts, audio/ audio-visual materials, artistic drawings, dictionaries

specific_competences.specific_competence: Evaluate the context in which literary texts are written, read and understood
learning_activities: (a) Assess the socio- political and cultural contexts in which the selected poems and plays were written
(b) Examine the socio- political, economic and cultural issues portrayed in selected poems and plays
(c) Relate the context of the story in selected poems and plays with real life experiences
teaching_methods: Information search: Guide the students through searching for information on the techniques to identify the setting of a poem and presenting their work to the class Group work: Guide the students through assessing the socio-political and cultural contexts of the selected poems and plays
Collaborative practice: Guide the students through examining the socio- political and economic issues portrayed in the selected poems and plays, and presenting their work to the class

Brainstorming: Guide the students in groups through brainstorming ideas on real-life experiences Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through identifying the context of the story in the selected poems and plays, relating such context with their life experiences and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: The socio- political and cultural contexts in which the selected poems and plays were written are assessed appropriately
The socio- political, economic and cultural issues portrayed in selected poems and plays are examined appropriately
The context of the story in selected poems and plays is related properly with real-life experiences
resources: A variety of literary texts, dictionaries

specific_competences.specific_competence: Analyse genres of literature and appreciate their conventions
learning_activities: (a) Describe different genres of written literature and their conventions
(b) Analyse techniques of critiquing poems and plays based on their conventions
(c) Critique selected poems and plays based on form and content
teaching_methods: Two Truths and a Lie: Guide the students through identifying genres of written literature through two truths and a lie Discussion/Group work: Guide the students in groups through describing different genres of written literature and their conversations. Then, guide each group through presenting its work to the class

Information search: Guide the students through searching for information about the techniques for critiquing poems and plays based on their conventions Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through sharing the information searched about the techniques for critiquing poems and plays, analysing the techniques and presenting them to the class

Brainstorming: Guide the students in pairs through brainstorming the elements of form and content in a literary work and presenting their work to the class Group work: Guide the students in groups critiquing poems and plays based on form and content
assessment_criteria: Different genres of literature and their conventions are described correctly
Techniques for critiquing poems and plays based on their conventions are analysed appropriately
Poems and plays are clearly critiqued based on form and content
resources: A variety of literary texts, dictionaries

specific_competences.specific_competence: Create simple literary works
learning_activities: (a) Compose free verse poems on various topics using literary language
(b) Publish the poems on various platforms (e.g., note boards and online platforms)
teaching_methods: Think-aloud-pair problem solving: Guide the students through Think-aloud- pair problem solving to explain steps in composing a poem Collaborative and independent practice: Guide the students in groups and individually through composing free verse poems on various topics using literary language
Publishing: Guide the students through publishing their poems composed on various platforms (e.g., note boards, or on the Internet)
assessment_criteria: Topics for composing poems are identified appropriately
Poems are published properly on various platforms
resources: Literary texts, audio/ audio-visual materials(audio/ video clips, recorded stories), artistic drawings, dictionaries

specific_competences.main_competence: Demonstrate mastery of English language skills
specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary in oral and in written language tasks
learning_activities: (a) Prepare and deliver short speeches about common topics (e.g., entrepreneurship, corruption, child rights and security, gender education, cyber security education, disaster management, health and reproductive education, drug abuse, life skills, financial management education, taxation)
(b) Compose different types of essays (narrative, descriptive, argumentative and expository) using correct grammar and vocabulary
teaching_methods: Project work: Ask the students to listen to various short speeches in their environment or from online sources and analyse them based on their characteristics, parts, the language used and techniques used in delivering such speeches. Presentation: Guide the students through presenting their work to the class Observation: Guide the students through observing and discussing the characteristics and language used in a given short speech on common topics Speech delivery: Guide the students through preparing short speeches on common topics and delivering such speeches to the class using appropriate techniques

Observation: Guide the students through observing and discussing the characteristics and language used in different types of essays. Then, let each group present its work to the class Composing/essay writing: Guide the students through composing different types of essays based on their characteristics
assessment_criteria: Short speeches about common topics are prepared and delivered appropriately
Different types of essays are composed using correct grammar and vocabulary
resources: Written texts of different types, dictionaries, encyclopaedia, oral texts, audio and audio- visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Read texts for comprehension
learning_activities: (a) Discuss the author’s motives in a given text
(b) Deliver an oral presentation about the content of a text
(c) Draw inferences (conclusions) from a text
teaching_methods: Close reading: Guide the students through identifying key ideas from a given text and presenting their work to the class Description: Guide the students through describing the author’s motives orally and in writing using the identified key ideas of the texts
Discussion: Guide the students through identifying and discussing the details of a given text and presenting their work to the class

Modelling: Use a text to show the students how to draw inferences (conclusions) Close reading: Guide the students through identifying the main details and facts from a given text and relating them with their experiences. Thereafter, guide them through drawing inferences (conclusions) and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: The author’s motives in the given text are discussed correctly
An oral presentation about the content of the text is made appropriately
Inferences (conclusions) are drawn correctly from the text
resources: Dictionaries, encyclopaedia, newspaper articles, journals

specific_competences.specific_competence: Comprehend oral messages with increasing difficulty
learning_activities: (a) Deduce the main ideas from an oral presentation or language task
(b) Examine information from oral sources
(c) Relate the core messages of an oral presentation to real life experiences
teaching_methods: Modelling: Play a recorded text/ speech to the students and show them how to deduce the main ideas from the text/speech Reading aloud: Ask another teacher to read aloud a text or deliver a speech while you listen to it attentively with your students. Then, show the students how to deduce the main ideas from such text/speech Speech delivery/Presentation: Deliver a speech/make a presentation to the students on common or cross-cutting topics using appropriate techniques and guide them through deducing the main ideas from the speech/presentation and presenting their work to the class

Pair work: Read aloud a story/ passage to the students and guide them in pairs through examining information from the story/ passage and presenting their work to the class Group work: Play a recorded text/speech to the students and guide them in groups through examining the information obtained in the text/speech and presenting their work to the class Project activity: Ask the students to listen to and watch the news on the radio and TV respectively at home or school. Then, ask them to examine the information from the news broadcast and present their work to the class

Group work: Guide the students in groups through discussing the content of a passage heard, identifying the core messages, relating such messages to their- life experiences and presenting their work to the class Pair work: Play a recorded text/ speech to the students and guide them in pairs through discussing its content, identifying the core messages, relating such messages to their life experiences and presenting their work to the class Project activity: Ask the students to listen to and watch the news on the radio and TV respectively at home and school. Then, ask them to examine the information from the news broadcast, relate it to their real-life experiences and present their work to the class
assessment_criteria: The main ideas from oral presentations and language tasks are deduced appropriately
Information from oral sources is examined appropriately
The core messages of the oral presentation are related correctly to real- life experiences
resources: Oral texts, audio and audio-visual materials (audio/video clips, recorded stories)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Construct meaning from a variety of texts
learning_activities: (a) Explore strategies for deriving meanings of words from given texts (e.g., contextual guessing)
(b) Synthesise ideas and draw conclusions from multiple and diverse texts
(c) Write a single text from information and opinions derived from a variety of texts
(d) Make inferences about a variety of texts
(e) Relate the core messages from multiple and diverse texts to real life experiences
teaching_methods: Exploration: Guide the students through exploring strategies for deriving meanings of words from texts and presenting their work to the class
Close reading: Guide the students through synthesising ideas and drawing conclusions from multiple and diverse texts, and presenting their work to the class
Close reading: Guide the students through using the main ideas and key messages and summaries from the texts read to write one text
Group work: Guide the students in groups through finding the details of the texts, using such details and personal knowledge to make inferences and presenting their work to the class

Close reading: Guide the students through reading texts, discussing their contents, identifying core messages, relating such messages to their real-life experiences and presenting their work to the class
assessment_criteria: Strategies for deriving meanings of words from given texts are explored appropriately
Ideas from multiple and diverse texts are synthesised correctly, and conclusions are drawn correctly
A single text from information and opinions derived from a variety of texts is written correctly
Inferences about a variety of texts are made appropriately
The core messages from multiple and diverse texts are related appropriately to real-life experiences
resources: Books, dictionaries, encyclopaedia, newspaper articles, journals

specific_competences.specific_competence: Use appropriate grammar and vocabulary for oral communication in a variety of contexts
learning_activities: (a) Express feelings and emotions depicted/ portrayed in various social contexts using appropriate phrases (e.g., I am saddened…, I am upset…, my condolences… I feel happy… hurray…)
(b) Deliver different kinds of planned and unplanned speeches (e.g., informative, persuasive speech) on different topics
(c) Negotiate solutions to various problems using appropriate formalaic language (e.g., Would you mind…, don’t you think…, is it possible…, if I were you…)
teaching_methods: Pictures: Display pictures/ emojis representing different feelings for students to describe orally what they represent Case study/Scenario: Provide the students with a case study/ scenario and ask them to express their feelings orally using appropriate phrases. Dialogue: Guide the students through acting out a dialogue with appropriate phrases for expressing feelings and emotions.

Discussion: Guide the students through discussing different types of speeches and presenting their work to the class Speech delivery: Guide the students through delivering planned and unplanned speeches

Roleplay: Guide the students through roleplaying negotiations to various problems using appropriate formulaic language Dialogue: Guide the students through reading aloud and acting out dialogues by negotiating solutions to various problems using appropriate formulaic language
assessment_criteria: Feelings and emotions depicted/ portrayed in various social contexts are expressed using appropriate phrases
Different kinds of planned and unplanned speeches on different topics are delivered properly
Solutions to various problems are negotiated using appropriate formulaic language
resources: Dictionaries, encyclopaedias, relevant texts (e.g., books for English grammar)

specific_competences.specific_competence: Create a variety of texts for different communicative purposes using the appropriate tone and register
learning_activities: (a) Write application letters for various purposes (e.g., job application, school admission)
(b) Write speeches on a variety of topics, including cross- cutting issues
(c) Write Curriculum Vitae (CV) for different purposes
teaching_methods: Information search: Guide the students through using various sources to search for information on the types and parts of application letters and presenting their work to the class Pair work: Guide the students in pairs through writing application letters for various purposes

Brainstorming: Guide the students through brainstorming the structure of speeches Demonstration: Demonstrate how to begin writing a speech by asking the students to give ideas and help you plan the speech Collaborative practice: Guide the students in pairs or groups through writing speeches on a variety of topics, including cross- cutting issues

Jigsaw: Guide the students through explaining the meaning, components and the importance of curriculum vitae using jigsaw Independent practice: Guide individual students through writing their CVs and sharing them in pairs for comments and improvement Publishing/storing: Guide the students in groups through storing or publishing their CVs on different platforms
assessment_criteria: Application letters for various purposes are written properly
Speeches on a variety of topics, including cross- cutting issues, are written properly
Curriculum Vitae (CV) for different purposes are written properly
resources: Dictionaries, encyclopaedia, relevant texts

specific_competences.specific_competence: Conduct a socio- cultural analysis of functional texts
learning_activities: (a) Analyse different functional texts in terms of purpose, content, organisation, format and design
(b) Read a variety of functional texts (e.g., recipes, product manuals, transport schedules, forms, brochures, and menus)
(c) Comment on the usefulness of different functional texts
(d) Compose functional texts to serve various purposes
teaching_methods: Jigsaw: Guide the students through the jigsaw to analyse different functional texts read (in terms of purpose, content, organisation, format and design)
Pair work: Provide the students in pairs with a variety of functional texts and guide them through reading the texts for comprehension
Group work: Guide the students in groups through commenting on the usefulness of the functional texts read and presenting their work to the class
Modelling: Engage the students by showing them how to compose various functional texts Composing: Guide the students through composing various functional texts
assessment_criteria: Different functional texts are analysed correctly in terms of purpose, content, organisation, format and design
A variety of functional texts are read effectively
The usefulness of different functional texts is commented on appropriately
Functional texts are composed properly to serve various purposes
